headline: Join the United States Space Force: 2026 Guardian Enlistment Guide
metaDescription: US Space Force recruitment 2026: age 17-42, ASVAB tiers, U.S. citizenship rule, 8.5-week BMT at Lackland, officer routes and Guardian career paths.

sections.content:
The United States Space Force is the newest US military branch, with roughly 16,000 personnel including about 8,000 civilians and no Guard or reserve component. Enlisted Guardians make up about half the force and work in space operations, cyber operations, intelligence, acquisitions and engineering support, mostly tied to ground stations and satellite missions.

Recruitment runs through local Air Force recruiters. Candidates take the ASVAB, are assessed against moral and physical standards, then visit the Military Entrance Processing Station for medical screening and job counseling. After qualifying, recruits enter the Delayed Entry Program while waiting for a Basic Military Training slot.
sections.title: The Guardian Path and Force Overview

sections.content:
Enlisted applicants must be 17 to 42 years old, with parental consent required at 17. Unlike the Air Force, enlisted Guardians must be US citizens rather than permanent residents. A high school diploma or GED equivalent is required.

The ASVAB standard is higher than the marketing floor suggests: Department of the Air Force policy sets an AFQT minimum of 36 for Tier 1 diploma holders and 50 for Tier 2 GED holders, though components may accept otherwise-qualified Tier 1 applicants at 31 or above. The Space Force is highly competitive, so real qualifying scores run well above the minimums.
sections.title: Eligibility: Age, Citizenship and ASVAB

sections.content:
Officers plan and manage Space Force personnel and make up about half the service because of its technical mission. Officer candidates must be 17 to 42, hold US citizenship, pass medical examinations and clear a background investigation. The Air Force Officer Qualifying Test is required for some routes.

The three commissioning paths are the US Air Force Academy, which offers free tuition in exchange for service, Air Force ROTC with scholarships at roughly 1,000 colleges, and Officer Training School for graduates. All lead to service in the Space Force's technical career fields.
sections.title: Becoming a Space Force Officer

sections.content:
Guardians attend 8.5 weeks of Basic Military Training at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland in Texas, the same BMT as Air Force recruits. The course covers military discipline, drill, physical conditioning and heritage, with 21 additional hours of Space Force-specific instruction on emotional intelligence, the service's organizational structure and doctrine.

After BMT, Guardians attend technical training school for their specialty before their first duty assignment. Career fields span orbital warfare, satellite communications, missile warning, cyber operations and space acquisitions, with promotion and pay matching the other armed services.
